questions.question: In which of the following classes does temperature determine the sex in some species?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Reptiles.__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Temperature determines the sex of some species of reptiles, such as crocodiles and turtles.
 
• This is known as temperature-dependent sex determination (TSD).
 
• The temperature at which the eggs are incubated determines whether they will develop into males or females.
 
• It is believed that the cortisol-mediated system and the epigenetic regulatory pathway are the possible mechanisms underlying TSD.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Mammals have genetic sex determination. Females have two X chromosomes, while males have one X and one Y chromosome.
 
• Aves (birds) also have genetic sex determination. The WZ system is used, where males have two Z chromosomes and females have one Z and one W chromosome.
 
• Amphibians have a variety of sex determination mechanisms. Some species have genetic sex determination, while others have environmental sex determination or a combination of both.

questions.question: Pipe A can fill a cistern in 6 hours and B can fill it in 30 hours. Both pipes were turned on but there was a leakage in the bottom of the cistern. So, the cistern took 30 minutes more to fill. The time that the leakage will take to empty the full cistern is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Pipe A fill a cistern in 6 hours

Pipe B fill a cistern in 30 hours

**Formula Used:**

Time = Total Work/Efficiency

**Calculation:**

Pipe A fill a cistern in 6 hours.

Pipe B fill a cistern in 30 hours.

Total units of water to be filled = LCM(6, 30) = 30 units.

Units of water filled by Pipe A in 1 hr = 5 units.

Units of water filled by Pipe A in 1 hr = 1 units.

Time taken to filled the tank = 30/(5 + 1) hours

⇒ 30/6 hours

⇒ 5 hours

 

With extra 30 minutes, the pipes would take 5 hours 30 minutes or 5.5 hours.

Let leakage can empty N units of water in 1 hour.

⇒ (5 + 1 - N) × 5.5 = 30

⇒ (6 - N) × 5.5 = 30

⇒ 6 - N = 30/5.5

⇒ 6 - N = 60/11

⇒ N = 6 - 60/11

⇒ N = 6/11

Leakage can empty 6/11 units of water in 1 hour.

Leakage can empty 30 unit of water = 30 × (11/6)

⇒ 330/6

⇒ 55 hours.

**∴ Time taken to empty the tank is 55 hours.**

questions.question: A sum of Rs. 4,800 is divided between A, B and C such that the ratio of the share of A to the combined share of B and C is 3 : 5 and C receives (5)/(7) of what A and B together receive. The difference (in Rs.) of A's share and B 's share is:

Total Sum with A, B and C = Rs. 4,800

**Calculation:-**

And,

⇒ C : (A + B) = 5 : 7 ……………………….(ii)

From eq(i), 

⇒ A’s share = 3x

⇒ (B + C)’s share = 5x

⇒ (A + B + C)’s share = 3x + 5x = 8x

From eq(ii), 

⇒ C’s share = 5X

⇒ (A + B)’s share = 7X

⇒ (A + B + C)’s share = 5x + 7x = 12x

To make the share equal in both equation, multiply eq(i) by 3 and eq(ii) by 2,

⇒ [A : (B + C) = 3 : 5] × 3

⇒ A : (B + C) = 9 : 15 …………………(iii)

⇒ [C : (A + B) = 5 : 7] × 2

⇒ C : (A + B) = 10 : 14 ………………..(iv)

From eq(iii) and (iv),

⇒ A = 9x

⇒ B = 5x

⇒ C = 10x

Difference between A’s share and B’s share = [(9x - 5x)/24x] × 4800

⇒ [4x/24x] × 4800

⇒ [1/6] × 4800

⇒ 800

**∴ Difference of A's share and B 's share is Rs. 800.**

questions.question: An object is placed in front of a concave mirror of focal length 12 cm, at a distance of 6 cm. Its image is formed at a distance of ________ and is_________.

__
 
• The given problem is related to the reflection of light by a concave mirror.
 
• The focal length of the mirror is given as 12 cm, and the object is placed at a distance of 6 cm from the mirror.
 
• Therefore, the object distance (u) is -6 cm (negative sign denotes that the object is placed in front of the mirror) and **f****ocal length (f) **is **negative** for concave mirror.
 
• To find the image distance (v), we can use the mirror formula: **1/f = 1/v + 1/u**, where f is the focal length of the mirror.
 
• Substituting the given values, we get** v = 12 cm.**
 
• The resulting image is magnified, erect, and** virtual.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Its surface has an inward curvature that makes it resemble the interior surface of a hollow sphere.
 
• The fact that they **induce light rays to converge**, or gather together after reflection, makes them **converging mirrors** as well.
 
• **Real and virtual image**s can be formed by an object and mirror placed in different positions.

questions.question: Which of the following are the end products of respiration in plants?

__
 
• **Respiration **is a process by which living organisms release energy from food molecules such as glucose.
 
• In plants, respiration occurs in mitochondria, which are organelles present in the cells.
 
• During respiration, **glucose is broken down **into smaller molecules such as pyruvate, which then undergo a series of chemical reactions **to produce CO2, water, and energy.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Respiration in Roots:**

 
• The plant's underground portion, the roots, take in air from the spaces and air gaps between the soil particles.
 
• The **oxygen that is taken up by the roots is used to release energy**, which is then employed to move minerals and salts out of the soil.
 
• This is the reason we frequently hear people warn against spending the night beneath a tree because the excess carbon dioxide that trees release after they breathe can cause **asphyxia.**

**Respiration in Stems:**

 
• In order for the stem to breathe, air diffuses into the stomata and travels through various cell regions.
 
• The released carbon dioxide is also dispersed via the stomata at this point.
 
• **Gaseous exchange is known to occur in lenticels **in woody or higher plants.

**Respiration in Leaves:**

 
• The minuscule openings in leaves are called stomata.
 
• **Every stomata is regulated by guard cells.**
 
• When the stoma between the inferior leaf and the atmosphere closes and opens, gases are exchanged.

__
 
• The amount of bending depends on the angle at which the light enters the new medium and the refractive index of the medium.
 
• Refracted light bends more in the direction of the normal line when it moves from a less dense material to a denser one.
 
• When a light beam passes from a **rarer medium into a denser medium**, its **angle of refraction is smaller than its angle of incidence.**
 
• When a light beam travels from an optically **denser medium to a rarer medium**, its **angle of refraction is always greater than its angle of incidence.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/dfa94ffab5642c85c209a077da4c3fb9444701f9c396538fa834b360699288d5.png] **

• It is used to reflect and analyze light. 
 
• A standard triangular prism can divide white light into its component colors, or what is known as a spectrum.
 
 
 
• The bending of light as it moves from one transparent substance into another is known as refraction.
 
 
• The bending caused by refraction allows us to create rainbows, prisms, magnifying glasses, and lenses.
 
• Our eyes are dependent on this light bending as well.

__
 
• When a **current-carrying wire is placed in a magnetic field**, a force is exerted on it due to the interaction between the magnetic field and the current.
 
• This force is perpendicular to both the magnetic field and the current direction and is given by the **right-hand rule**.
 
• Since the north pole of the magnet is facing upwards, the force direction is reversed due to the negative charge of electrons in the wire, which results in the wire deflecting towards the south direction.
 
• The electrons are flowing from **west to east.**
 
• [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/db02749044689370143951d12e1c574f50f296ef6aef76c54f0cb416e6a5b7f1.png]

• This rule is frequently applied as a mnemonic to **help remember the way the three axes—X, Y, and Z**—orient on a three-dimensional plane.
 
• It says that when we position our right hand's thumb, forefinger, and middle finger perpendicular to one another, then:
 
 
• The thumb indicates the **direction in which the conductor is moving in relation to the magnetic field**.
 
• The **direction of the magnetic field** is shown by the forefinger.
 
• The middle finger is pointing in the** induced current's direction.**

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a part of aggregate demand in an economy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Increase in population.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Aggregate demand** is the total demand for goods and services in an economy at a given time.
 
• It **comprises four components**: consumption, investment, government spending, and net exports.
 
• **Increase in population is not a part of aggregate demand.**
 
• **Consumption **refers to the spending by households on goods and services.
 
 
• It is the largest component of aggregate demand.
 
 
 
• **Investment** includes spending by businesses on capital goods such as machinery, equipment, and buildings.
 
 
• It also includes spending on research and development and the creation of new businesses.
 
 
 
• **Government spending** includes all the expenditures made by the government on goods and services, such as defense, education, healthcare, and infrastructure.
 
• **Net exports** refer to the difference between the value of exports and imports.
 
 
• When the value of exports is greater than imports, it is called a **trade surplus**, and when the value of imports is greater than exports, it is called a **trade deficit.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Imports** are a part of aggregate demand as they **represent the spending by households, businesses, and the government on foreign goods and services.**
 
• **Capital goods** are a part of aggregate demand as they **represent the spending by businesses** on the production of goods and services.
 
• **Exports** are a part of aggregate demand as they **represent the demand for goods and services** from foreign countries.

questions.question: Two resistors, each of 10 Ω, are connected in parallel. The combination, in turn, is connected in series to a third resistor of 10 Ω and a battery of 6 V. The power supplied by the battery is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __2.4 W.__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The two resistors of 10 Ohms each are connected in parallel.
 
• The **equivalent resistance** of two resistances R1 and R2 connected in parallel is given by** R1R2/(R1+R2).**
 
• It would result in an equivalent resistance of 5 Ohms.
 
• The 5 Ohm equivalent resistance is connected in series with a third resistor of 10 Ohm, resulting in a total resistance of 15 Ohm.
 
• Using Ohm's law, we can find the current flowing through the circuit, which is** I = V/R = 6/15 = 0.4 A.**
 
• Finally, the power supplied by the battery is given by **P = VI = 6 x 0.4 = 2.4 W.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The equivalent resistance is less than either of the individual resistances when two resistors are connected in parallel.
 
• This is because the total current flowing through the circuit is divided between the two resistors, and each resistor experiences a smaller voltage drop.
 
• The equivalent resistance of two resistances R1 and R2 connected in parallel is given by R1R2/(R1+R2).
 
• The total current in each branch of a parallel circuit is known as the total current.
 
 
• It is given by: I = I1 + I2 + I3+...+In
 
 
 
• The voltage across each branch and the total voltage of a parallel circuit have the same value.
 
 
• It is expressed as: ET = E1 = E2 = E3 =... = EN.
